name: New Orleans
tagline: Jazz, Creole food and the French Quarter
summary: The birthplace of jazz, with iron-balconied streets in the French Quarter, live music on Frenchmen Street, oak-lined streetcar rides through the Garden District and Creole and Cajun food like nowhere else. Mardi Gras and Jazz Fest are among the world's great parties.
seasonNote: Mardi Gras (February or March) and Jazz Fest (late April to early May) are peak. Summers are hot and humid, and hurricane season runs June to November.
arrival: Louis Armstrong International Airport is about 25 minutes from the French Quarter.
gettingAround: Walk the Quarter and Marigny; streetcars run along St. Charles Avenue and Canal Street.
cashTip: Cards work widely; carry small bills to tip street musicians.
foodTip: Beignets, gumbo, jambalaya, po'boys, crawfish in spring and Creole fine dining.
buyTip: Hot sauce, pralines, Mardi Gras masks and vintage from Magazine Street.
baseArea: French Quarter or Marigny for music; Garden District for quieter streets
